title: Late Breaking Results: Hybrid Logic Optimization with Predictive Self-Supervision
problem: Logic synthesis optimization methods are typically application-agnostic, but different circuit regions benefit from different optimization techniques; identifying optimal region-specific methods requires expensive simulation.
motivation: Hybrid logic optimization can achieve superior results by applying diverse methods to different circuit regions, but requires identifying the best method per region which is computationally expensive without effective predictive models.
method: They extract vertex features—metrics describing each circuit region's local structure and compatibility with different optimization methods—by analyzing subgraph neighborhoods and testing how various optimization approaches perform. They use these features to partition the circuit into clusters, applying each cluster's optimal optimization method. To avoid expensive testing, they use self-supervised learning to predict these vertex features for any circuit region, enabling rapid hybrid optimization without simulation.
key_novelty: A self-supervised learning model predicts vertex features describing optimization-method compatibility, enabling rapid circuit partitioning and hybrid optimization without expensive simulation.
contributions: Subgraph-based vertex feature extraction quantifying compatibility with different optimization methods
Self-supervised prediction model reducing feature computation cost
Circuit partitioning method clustering regions by optimal optimization approach achieving 8.48% area and 9.81% delay improvement
limitations: Specific baseline names and scalability to very large circuits not detailed.
primary_theme: Hybrid logic optimization via self-supervised region identification
